title: engine-plan.v1 — one immutable revision of a plan under deliberation, wrapping the exact Build payload
description: The plan document the Project Manager mints, revises, and eventually seals. It is JSON and only JSON: there is no YAML working copy, no uncheckpointed-edit state, and no checkpoint verb — a revision is minted whole by `revise` and never edited in place, so the digest over its canonical form is the plan's identity. Two halves. The DELIBERATION half is the reasoning a Build cannot reconstruct: what problem this solves, the strongest case against doing it, the alternatives and why each was disposed of, how it could fail, and what remains undecided. The BUILD half is `build_plan` — the byte-exact payload the Build Coordinator will consume at `plan bind`, carried whole rather than re-derived, so a sealed plan and the Build it authorizes can never describe different work. NOTE ON `build_plan`, and please do not 'improve' it: it is deliberately typed as a bare object here with no properties, no required list, and no additionalProperties rule. Its authority belongs to the Build Coordinator, not to this schema — plan_contract.validate_document delegates to build_coordinator_dag.validate_plan_document, which applies the coordinator's own three layers (its schema for the declared version, work-item-id uniqueness, and DAG closure) against the same code path `plan bind` runs. Re-expressing any of those rules here would create a second notion of a valid payload that could drift from the first, and the drift would surface as a plan that seals cleanly and then fails at bind.

allOf.title: The imported-draft allowance
allOf.description: A plan that arrived as an accepted native Claude or Codex plan has not been deliberated here and has not been decomposed here, and the honest thing for it to say is nothing. Everywhere else the deliberation prose carries a non-empty floor, because a plan that cannot frame its problem or state the case against itself has not been thought about. An import is the one case where that floor would produce the opposite of what it is for: the only way to satisfy it at import time is to write placeholder prose, and placeholder prose in `case_against` is precisely the decoy that field's own description warns is worse than an empty one. So the floor is stated as a conditional instead of as a base rule, keyed on the payload the import carries (`build-plan.imported`, which forbids a non-empty decomposition for the same reason). The exception is not a hole: an imported draft must carry `intake` saying where it came from, and must record at least one `unresolved_decisions` entry — the gaps, named as gaps. Since the seal refuses while any unresolved decision remains, and `build-plan.imported` can never be sealed, an imported draft cannot reach a Build until someone actually does the work this allowance declines to fake.

plan_id.description: Minted once at `init` and never reissued — not by revision, not by retitling, not by clone (a clone mints its own). The folder slug is a convenience for humans; this is the identity.

revision.description: Monotonic from 1. Revisions are immutable and every one is kept: the ledger is the record of how the plan got here, and a reader who only ever sees the head cannot tell a settled decision from a reversed one.

revision_note.description: What changed in this revision and why — written for the operator reading the ledger months later, not for the tool.

raw.description: What the operator actually said, kept verbatim. Never tidied, never paraphrased into the interpretation: the gap between the two is exactly what a reviewer needs to see.

case_against.description: The strongest honest argument for NOT doing this, stated at its full weight. A plan that cannot state one has not been deliberated; a decoy here is worse than an empty field, because it launders the absence of thought. Non-empty is REQUIRED and enforced in this schema's `allOf` below — the floor lives there, not here, only so that the one case that may leave it empty (an imported native plan, which has not been deliberated here and must not pretend otherwise) can be stated as an explicit exception rather than as a hole in the base shape.

unresolved_decisions.description: Open questions the operator still owes an answer to. The array may be non-empty for as long as the plan is a draft; the seal refuses while any entry remains, which is the whole point of recording them.

operator_decisions.description: Decisions the operator made by name, kept so a later session cannot quietly re-litigate a settled call.

intake.description: Where this plan came from when it did not start here — an imported native Claude or Codex plan, or prose drafts that preceded it. Groundwork, not authority: an import lands as an unapproved draft with its gaps marked as gaps.

program.description: Optional linkage into a multi-PR program (engine-program.v1). Absent for a standalone plan, and absent is the normal case — a plan is per-Build, and a program is a deliberate act, never inferred from resemblance.

build_plan.description: The exact Build payload, carried whole. Intentionally unconstrained here — see the note in this schema's own description before adding any rule to this object.

intent_source.description: Mirrors build-plan.v2's own intent_source shape, because an unattended (Routine) Build still draws its AUTHORIZATION from a durable Issue even once the plan authority is local.

carried_obligation.description: An obligation handed forward from a predecessor plan. `released` is the escape hatch, and the stated reason is its entire price: the guarantee was never that obligations get met, only that one can never be dropped silently. Until now that price was collected by convention — the reason field was optional, the projection printed '(no reason given)' when it was missing, and nothing refused. So the escape hatch had a quieter escape hatch inside it, and the one release that mattered would have been the one nobody wrote a reason for. The conditional above makes it mechanical for every future release rather than something asserted about the ones already written: `released` without a reason does not validate, and the program library refuses the same shape at add_child, so neither the plan nor the program record can carry a release nobody explained.
